habitat: Usually singly in a variety of wooded habitats, including well-wooded suburbia.
summary: A common summer resident, with some present all year. The male is bright green above and white below, with a white mark behind the eye only, no white in the wing, a dark eye, a green bill and white outer tail feathers. The female is duller, green above and white below with heavy brown banding, and has a yellow eye. The call is a mournful hueet-jie, five or six times. Months were left unset. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Diederik Cuckoo has white marks before and behind the eye, a white crown stripe and white marks on the wings, plus a red eye and a black bill.
Female African Emerald Cuckoo lacks the white mark behind the eye and is more bronze above, with heavier barring below.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^14=16384 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 8192–32768.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

head.pattern: A white mark behind the eye only.

underparts.pattern: Heavily banded brown. Finer and darker below than female African Emerald Cuckoo.

viewNotes.note: Green above and white below, with a white mark behind the eye and no white in the wing.
White underparts and a dark eye. The bill is green.
Entirely bright green above, from the bill to the tail.
No white wing markings. The upperwing is green.
White below, with white outer tail feathers.

calls.description: A mournful hueet-jie, repeated five or six times. Newman does not separate the sexes. Grade A song from Kruger National Park. The filename is KlaassCuckooKruger2007-01-08.mp3.

research.note: Newman says common summer resident, some present all year, and does not name months. Status is summer-migrant and months were left unset, so the year-round birds are not shown as present in winter. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged. Population figures were left unchanged.
